indicators.notes: Stale contextual city-limit accounting-core measurement: the official City CAP Appendix A identifies 2019 as the latest available Carmel community inventory (printed pp. 2–4; Table B is printed p. 4 / physical PDF page 8). The narrative scope definitions are on printed p. 3 / physical PDF page 7. Table B reports 30,962 metric tons CO2e as “Total Scope 1 Emissions” and 46,076 as “Total with Scope 3 Emissions.” The CAP's own prose defines Scope 2 as indirect emissions from electricity generation, yet Table B adds residential/commercial electricity (63+92 MT) into the 30,962 subtotal labeled Scope 1. This finding calls 30,962 the CAP accounting-core total excluding its separately reported Scope 3 travel; it is not a technically strict Scope 1 total. That core also includes travel occurring within Monterey County even when the trip originates outside the City, as well as solid waste and wastewater; it is not a strict city-territorial or full consumption inventory. The CAP identifies added Scope 3 as vehicle travel outside Monterey County and excludes those emissions from target-setting (printed pp. 3, 6); thus 46,076 is not a complete value-chain inventory either. As context, 46,076 ÷ 3,811 = 12.09 tCO2e/resident/year if the City-reported Scope 3 travel is included. indicators.name: Mapped natural-vegetation-to-developed gross conversion proxy
indicators.source: Derived 2014–2024 whole-county pixel transitions: USGS Annual NLCD C1.1 via official USDA Forest Service/GeoPlatform service
indicators.notes: Derived mapped gross conversion, 2014–2024, not a field-survey estimate, not total developed/impervious share, not native-only habitat loss, and not net land loss after restoration. Tier 1 City/County planning, forest assessment, GIS and TAMC RCIS did not provide a current exact decadal conversion statistic; FMMP farmland conversion was rejected. Tier 2 USGS Annual NLCD Collection 1.1 was accessed through the official USDA Forest Service/GeoPlatform ImageServer. Catalog raster IDs 30 and 40 are Annual_NLCD_LndCov_2014_CU_C1V1 and Annual_NLCD_LndCov_2024_CU_C1V1. Both exports preserve the same original 30 m WGS84 Albers grid, unrendered U8 classes and nearest-neighbor resampling; they are not screenshots or interpolated cover percentages. Natural-land crosswalk uses the terrestrial classes in EPA's published Wisconsin Integrated Assessment Table 1 (2014; PDF p.22): forest 41/42/43, shrub52, non-intensively-managed grass/herb71 and wetlands90/95. Water11 is omitted because this indicator is land conversion; pasture81 and crops82 are omitted. Barren31 is omitted in that published crosswalk because it combines natural bare surfaces and mined areas. This is an explicit operational natural-cover definition, not a claim that every natural dune or beach is represented; the Wisconsin report is method support, not Monterey observations. The classification definitions are checked against the current MRLC legend. Applying all classes31/12 as natural instead yields 0.21987428971596729%/decade; a pixel-center boundary rule gives 0.21719657042855467%/decade. Both remain below the configured 0.5 threshold. No snow12 occurs here. Numerator is the area of pixels in natural classes in 2014 and developed21–24 in 2024, intersected with the same current whole-county boundary for both years; denominator is 2014 natural-class area. Fractional boundary pixels use geometric intersection area. This is 15431398.708466765 m² / 7109372039.741001 m² ×100 = 0.21705712715843378% per 10-year period. No city rates are averaged, and all incorporated/unincorporated county land is included. The archived current Census county boundary and 2026 TIGER Faces LWFLAG='P' perennial-water exclusion define a fixed reporting footprint, not historical jurisdiction changes. An unobserved 0.5623719223487662m² coastal sliver remains; it is reported, excluded from observed classes, and never recoded as zero conversion. This is less than 1m² of 8499610994.628198m² county land. Raster-vs-polygon land-area integration differs by 5.633291244506836m² (~6.6e-10 relative), retained as numerical/boundary sliver tolerance. Classification errors, 30m mixed pixels and development's open-space class limit accuracy; no local transition accuracy or statistical confidence interval is available. Raw rasters, source requests, hashes, boundary inputs, exact area weights, class transitions, sensitivities and offline calculate.py are preserved in calculations/land-conversion. The image-service browser capture returned403; the existing capture helper archived original JSON bytes, and reviewed faithful metadata/derived-table exhibits supply the visible evidence.
indicators.review_note: Independently refetched official 2014/2024 Annual NLCD TIFFs and both native-grid records: byte-identical to archives; live catalog IDs 30/40 confirm the two C1V1 years. Offline calculate.py rerun in a temporary copy reproduces 15,431,398.708466765 / 7,109,372,039.741001 × 100 = 0.21705712715843378% per decade and canonical round1 score -56.6. Same 30 m equal-area grid, exact fractional county-boundary weights, perennial-water mask, observed-class denominator and 0.562371922 m² unobserved sliver treatment were checked. Wisconsin EPA crosswalk and MRLC legend support the declared vegetation classes but do not establish all coastal natural land: including ambiguous barren class 31 gives 0.21987428971596729%, and pixel-center weighting gives 0.21719657042855467%. Final display explicitly labels this mapped gross-conversion proxy with medium confidence, no native-only or net-restoration claim; classification/mixed-pixel/local-accuracy limitations remain. The calculation covers all incorporated and unincorporated county resident land on the fixed current footprint. Final labelled derived exhibit visually inspected; pass applies to this operational mapped proxy, not field-verified complete habitat loss.

indicators.notes: Derived 2024 mapped inventory, not a jurisdiction-published total or a complete legal parcel audit. Older 2023 records sharing this service are explicitly excluded. More recent 2026 data was investigated and rejected for this derivation: its geometries mix GAP classes, with partial conserved-acre fields and qualifying portions inside GAP3/4 units; precise jurisdiction clipping would need their underlying subgeometry. No partial 2026 fractions are imputed to city land. Jurisdiction: all incorporated and unincorporated Monterey County, current Census TIGERweb GEOID 06053, retrieved 2026-10-23. The 2024 conservation inventory is evaluated against current retrieved boundaries and Census 2026 perennial-water faces; it is not a claim about conservation gains through 2026. Exclude LWFLAG=P water (ocean, bays, lakes, other perennial water) from numerator and denominator; retain intermittent water under Census land convention. WGS84 GeoJSON and NAD83 Census water are transformed to California Albers EPSG:3310 using the null NAD83/WGS84 geographic transform at this precision. Union protected polygons before measuring clipped area; overlaps count once. Numerator=1564208099.145379305 m² (386524.239033349 acres), denominator=8499610982.289926529 m² (2100299.614101260 acres). 2,125 candidate features downloaded completely; 1,316 belong to Release_Year=2024; 517 intersect jurisdiction land. Union removes 754.581983 m² of overlapping protected polygons. Land denominator differs from Census AREALAND=8,499,610,214 m² by 768 m² (0.000009%), consistent with projection/rounding. Source uncertainty includes generalized boundaries and omitted/misclassified conservation; confidence medium. All raw query URLs/hashes, compressed polygons, per-feature areas and offline script are archived in calculations/biodiversity-loss/. Primary exhibit is labelled our derived calculation; official dataset, methodology, boundary and water-definition captures are supplemental.

indicators.name: Extreme heat exposure
indicators.source: Derived from CDC/ATSDR Environmental Justice Index 2024: 2018–2022 extreme-heat days and ACS population
indicators.notes: Observation period: 2018–2022 annual average; year=2022 is the period end, not a single-year count. Derived resident-weighted county exposure summary: sum(E_NEHD × E_TOTPOP) / sum(E_TOTPOP) = 6,351,206.4 / 437,609 = 14.513427283259714 days/year. All 103 Monterey County tracts included in CDC EJI 2024; Census 2020 lists 104 county tracts, with water-only zero-population tract 06053990000 absent from EJI. The remaining 103 cover the county resident land geography. No residents are removed by this water-tract omission. This is an observed membership difference; CDC documentation does not state a removal policy. CDC EJI 2024 E_NEHD is the annual mean for 2018–2022, computed as the five-year sum divided by five. The included dictionary defines a day as maximum temperature exceeding the tract-specific historical 95th percentile; this is a relative local-temperature criterion. Weights E_TOTPOP are 2018–2022 ACS S0601 population estimates from the same package. Both fields agree across all 103 tracts between the official CSV package and CDC data service; none is missing or negative. This is a weighted mean of tract annual means, not the number of days when the entire county simultaneously exceeded a threshold, an absolute-temperature count, heat-index count, NWS HeatRisk, or future projection. CDC crosswalked heat from 2010 to 2020 tracts; nationally 13 missing tracts were interpolated but the local interpolation status is not identified. The EJI heat entry does not specify historical baseline years or seasonal window; do not import a baseline from Cal-Adapt or another CDC series. Tract annual means range 6.8–18.4. Source tier 1 searched: Carmel 2021 vulnerability assessment and 2022 adaptation plan give modeled baseline and projections (>87.9°F), not a recent observed city series; the county economic report gives 2010–2024 mean nine days >=92.5°F but its Cal-Adapt observed/projected split is insufficiently documented for acceptance. County 2026 public draft climate plan provides old historical baselines and projections. Tier 2 official retrospective CDC EJI series accepted; direct CDC Tracking county API requests were rate-limited (429), not treated as evidence of no data. Reproduction and raw hash manifest are in calculations/extreme-heat/.
indicators.unscored_reason: No adopted or scientifically defensible safe annual number of locally extreme-temperature days was established. The 95th-percentile rule defines an exposure event; it is not a safe annual-day target. Historical climatological averages, forecast HeatRisk categories, occupational exposure limits and zero days are not adopted annual targets for this measure.
indicators.review_note: Independently refetched official CDC EJI 2024 ZIP in preceding review (SHA256 b31f0610997df43e75d2e84e60689d7a6ee4cba19eba03912411ff3e4ba278ca) and confirmed all 103 live heat/population pairs. Repeated corrected offline derivation and independently checked Decimal arithmetic:6,351,206.4/437,609=14.513427283259714 days/year for 2018–2022, not 2022 alone. Corrected notes/exhibit now match independently archived Census 2020 coverage:104 tracts, with sole omitted 06053990000 having zero population/housing/land and 1,141,754,797 m² water; no CDC removal policy inferred. Pass is a population-weighted mean of tract annual means covering incorporated/unincorporated resident land, not simultaneous countywide events.
